name: Black Jack
summary: Black Jack from one deck against WOPR's dealer. You sit down with $100 and bet $1 to $25 a hand.
howToPlay: Get closer to 21 than the dealer without going over. Number cards count their number, faces count 10, and an ace counts 1 or 11. An ace and a ten-count card as your first two cards is a black jack, which pays 3 to 2.
At YOUR BET: type a whole number of dollars from 1 to 25. Press Enter on an empty line to bet the same as last time.
Then type H to hit (take a card) or S to stand. The prompt also offers D to double down and P to split when your hand and your money allow them.
Doubling down doubles your bet and gives you exactly one more card. Splitting turns a pair of the same rank into two hands, once a round; split aces get one card each.
The dealer checks for black jack when it shows an ace or a ten-count card, draws to 17, and stands on soft 17.
Type LEAVE at YOUR BET: to cash out. The game also ends when you have less than $1.

controls.does: at YOUR BET:, bet $10 (whole dollars, 1 to 25)
at YOUR BET:, bet the same as last time
keep your hand as it is
double your bet and take one last card (first two cards only)
split a pair into two hands (once a round)
at YOUR BET:, cash out and end the game
leave the table and go back to WOPR

tips: Stand on 13 to 16 when the dealer shows a 2 to 6, and hit them when it shows 7 or higher. The dealer must draw to 17, so a low card showing often means it busts.
Double down on 11, and on 10 unless the dealer shows a ten-count card or an ace.
Always split aces and eights. Never split tens or fives.
The deck is not shuffled every hand: WOPR deals from one deck until fewer than 15 cards are left, then says WOPR SHUFFLES THE DECK. When many tens and aces are still to come, bet more.

screenshots.caption: The first hand is a black jack: an ace and a king win $15 on a $10 bet.
A pair of eights split into two hands against the dealer's 6. WOPR asks about HAND 1 first.
The dealer draws the QC and busts. The doubled first hand wins $50 and the second $25, for $200.
